newsitem.title: LATVIA: FOCUS-Estonia bourse is Baltic star again.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Estonia bourse is Baltic star again.

text.p: Booming Estonian shares left Baltic neighbours Latvia and Lithuania standing over the last week although Lithuania saw one of its best.
Dealers in all three markets saw the same trend continuing into next week.
Analysts say the Estonian market surge is backed by sound fundamentals after a positive first-half results and raised 1997 profit forecasts, some above expectations, from leading banks.
The market was also still reacting to the European Commission's decision to invite Estonia to entry talks in a first wave of expansion.
Estonia's surge is reinforced by a real lack of liquidity on the small market, dealers say.
Lithuania made modest gains, with the blue chips of the official list leading the way.
ESTONIA
The Talse index ended the week at 422.09, a new high, versus 363.53 at the end of last week.
"I see no reason why the same rises that took place this week should not happen next week," said one trader.
Leading shares Hansapank and Hoiupank also maintained their sharp gains. Hansa ended the week at 233.50 kroons versus 201.88 while Hoiu closed at 270 kroons compared with 225 kroons.
LATVIA
Shares failed to move out of their summer-inspired lull, trading in a narrow range with few large price movements.
The bourse index ended the week at 384.24 versus 388.64 at the end of last week.
A new system of trading, allowing investors to buy and sell shaes in an unlimited quantity after the morning price fix rather than in limited amouts, failed to give much of a boost.
"I do not think the market will move much next week, it may stay at around the same levels," said one trader.
Leading share Unibanka was most traded during the week but ended lower at 3.31 lats compared with 3.35 lats.
LITHUANIA
Shares were also sleepy but showed more signs of life during the week, with a modest rally.
The official list index of leading blue chip shares ended the week at 1096.05 versus 1017.71.
"Generally, I think there will be some stabilisation in prices of blue chips, maybe with a slight increase," said Arvydas Jacikevichius, a broker with Suprema.
"There won't be such big increases of prices as there were this week," Jasikevichius said.
Hermis Bank ended the week at 265 versus 250.20 litas while leading bank Vilniaus Bankas was at 300 versus 260 litas. -- Riga newsroom, +371 721 5240
